map.[sod] - pasti.guards.10.41.0.message: So you will not leave us alone!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.13.20.0.message: This box may contain something useful for your mission.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.13.25.0.message: You are in our forest, friend, and we do not like it at all.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.14.25.0.message: Sounds from the beautiful countryside ahead interrupt your ride. Are you imagining things? You cannot let it go, and ponder what to do. Continue, or return to the fortress for fresh reinforcements? IT IS ALL UP TO YOU.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.2.34.0.message: You will not get rid of us!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.2.57.0.message: So many boxes. Could this be a trap? Perhaps they belonged to those shipwrecks. It might be worth investigating.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.21.7.0.message: Show us what you are made of!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.22.19.0.message: Another unclaimed box. Who might be guarding it, and what might be inside?
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.26.18.0.message: I take my hat off to you. You are doing very well so far.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.27.29.0.message: You are entering holy ground. Take care; your journey could end here.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.27.41.0.message: At last, you see a little pile of riches.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.3.31.0.message: So you just will not listen.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.32.57.0.message: There really seems to be no one here.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.37.56.0.message: You have discovered a sacred town, a town of wise sages. Yet it is suspiciously quiet. Something is wrong here.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.4.38.0.message: What is that? Surely your eyes are not deceiving you. Who could have destroyed such a beautiful forest? It must have been those evil goblins.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.4.68.0.message: You might get through this way.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.42.28.0.message: Beware of Adrienne, ruler of the dragons. She could be somewhere nearby.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.47.26.0.message: Those were some battles. You deserve a reward.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.5.17.0.message: This treasure belongs to us, and we will not give it to you.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.52.31.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.52.33.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.54.30.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.54.32.0.message: Now you have gone too far!! You should never have reached this place. Very well, you asked for it.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.54.34.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.54.51.0.message: You see a house. Who might live there?
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.56.30.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.56.32.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.56.34.0.message: You have trespassed on our sacred ground.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.58.40.0.message: The library before you belongs to me. If you wish to pass, you must first fight my company.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.6.39.0.message: You will pass this way only over our dead bodies!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.60.60.1.message: Only a truly skilled warrior may enter here.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.63.41.0.message: Be careful here. This rock city is hundreds of years old. Rumour has it that hideous monsters dwell here and could do your company harm.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.66.53.0.message: You just will not leave us alone!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.67.29.1.message: You are in a very dangerous area. WATCH OUT!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.69.42.0.message: Where are you off to, soldier boy? You are going the wrong way.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.70.39.1.message: So this is where those horrible woodcutters live, those destroyers of forests. Finish them once and for all.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.70.47.0.message: Did you not understand? YOU ARE GOING THE WRONG WAY!!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.8.28.0.message: So you just will not listen.
map.[sod] - pasti.guards.8.40.0.message: You will pass this way only over our dead bodies!!!!
map.[sod] - pasti.header.description: It is up to you to stop the barbarians from ravaging your land once and for all. Be careful: the snares and traps you encounter could prove very painful. Your scouts have learned that you need only capture Malice, the stronghold belonging to the cruel barbarian.
map.[sod] - pasti.header.name: Traps
map.[sod] - pasti.header.rumor.0.text: It is up to you to stop the barbarians from ravaging your land once and for all. Be careful: the snares and traps you encounter could prove very painful. Your scouts have learned that you need only capture Malice, the stronghold belonging to the cruel barbarian.
map.[sod] - pasti.header.rumor.1.text: His loyal subjects firmly believe that powerful, invincible magic protects the castle and its troops.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.10.0.0.message: Want to see a trick? Take me into your company and you will see what I can do.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.11.1.0.message: Where are you!! I cannot hold this orb any longer.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.14.1.0.message: Gentlemen, how long must I wait for you?
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.14.49.0.messag: How did you get here? This town belongs to us. Defend yourself, miserable worm.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.20.9.0.message: Why are you bothering us? We have something important to guard here. If you do not leave me alone, I will call my mates.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.4.1.0.message: Where have you been all this time, my commander?
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.42.51.0.messag: You are gambling with your life.
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.55.41.0.messag: My commander, I am waiting here for you. May I join you?
map.[sod] - pasti.monster.6.1.0.message: I may be rather old, but I think I can be useful to you.
map.[sod] - pasti.quest.13.40.0.complete: At last! With the help of 15 Black Dragons, we shall protect our kingdom! Here is your reward. Are the warriors ready to leave?
map.[sod] - pasti.quest.13.40.0.firstVis: I am an agent of the emperor of a distant land. His armies recently suffered a crushing defeat. If you brought me 15 Black Dragons, I could reward you well.
map.[sod] - pasti.quest.13.40.0.nextVisi: No luck finding 15 Black Dragons? Please hurry! Our kingdom’s fate is in your hands.
map.[sod] - pasti.quest.29.51.0.firstVis: In the old days, powerful wizards could create magical artifacts. But the evil phoenixes drove all my friends to abandon the town in fear of those winged monsters, leaving me here alone. If you could defeat the evil phoenixes and take one of those old artifacts from them, restoring our power, I would reward you well.
map.[sod] - pasti.quest.29.51.0.nextVisi: Still nothing? I am sure you will find the Vial of Dragon Blood soon. Please keep looking.
map.[sod] - pasti.sign.2.1.0.message: Explore this area thoroughly, and above all, make use of this luck so you will not miss it later.
map.[sod] - pasti.town.2.7.0.event.0.des: For your great courage, I have built you a Portal of Glory. Keep up the good work, and I shall be pleased with you.
map.[sod] - pasti.town.2.7.0.event.1.des: You are good. You deserve another reward.
map.[sod] - pasti.town.2.7.0.event.3.des: Your subjects have built more buildings for your courage. CONGRATULATIONS:
map.[sod] - pasti.town.3.33.1.event.0.de: Your subjects have constructed a building in honour of your valour.
map.[sod] - pasti.town.4.2.1.name: Malice
map.[sod] - pomsta mnichu.header.descrip:
Years ago, the kings of this land robbed the monks’ tombs.
Now the monks are preparing their revenge.  They intend to spare no one.
map.[sod] - pomsta mnichu.header.name: Revenge of the Monks
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.0.description:
This is my first map. I have tried to develop it thoroughly so you can enjoy it as much as possible. Send any comments or suggestions for improving it to my email address
{Kuchi.2.@seznam.cz}. I hope you enjoy it to the full and that you like it.
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.1.description: Something terrible must have happened here. Everything is empty, with not a building or a person in sight. Very strange indeed.
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.2.description:
A few little tips: Never rush anything; read and listen carefully.
                                   Never give up. If you die, try again and                                           again.
                                   Good Luck – Good Luck
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.3.description: Ignore the errors the editor reports when you press SHIFT + V. They add a little variety.
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.4.description: At last you have returned home. In five years, you had forgotten what it looked like. Many honourable, devoted soldiers died on your journey to the eastern Atlantic, where you went to help a small country called Gondlha. Now, however, you look forward to seeing your parents and your castle—and above all, to your coronation.
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.5.description: The infernal creatures are spreading further. We must stop them immediately.
map.[sod] - pomsta.event.6.description: The elves come to greet you and give you some gifts.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.100.80.0.messa: Now left, and straight to my castle.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.101.14.0.messa: You are here. It is quite repulsive, and reeks of sulfur and smoke.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.102.93.0.messa: Where are the buildings? Where is everyone? Why is it so quiet? This is very strange.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.103.66.0.messa: But I will show them. I swear to avenge my people. I SWEAR.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.103.85.0.messa: No buildings, no one anywhere. Where is everyone? And that silence… I will go mad.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.106.42.0.messa: “There it is! There it is!” You had almost given up hope. Before you rises a castle straight out of a fairy tale. It even holds the Grail…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.106.60.0.messa: A harbour, but it is in a terrible state too. Still, I do not give up so easily.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.107.22.0.messa: You chose correctly. I can see your father’s blood runs in your veins.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.107.25.0.messa: You find yourself in a strange place, surrounded by the dead and their bones. You remember your father telling you about a famous, highly developed castle called Smrtak. This place certainly looks the part.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.107.28.0.messa: Castle Smrtak is famous for its walls and inaccessibility. If I capture it, victory is mine.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.107.33.0.messa: Perhaps it is here. If I captured it, then…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.11.34.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.11.45.0.messag: You have just found a huge bandit supply depot. Men in ragged clothing swarm around a little shop marked “Black Market”.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.11.64.0.messag: You have a strong will, my friend, so I will give you a little gift.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.12.19.0.messag: You dared enter this territory. You must die.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.12.86.0.messag: The hardworking little sprites are already busy in the mill, but they look very tired. You ask whether they would like a break. Feeling sorry for them, you offer to take over for a while. They thank you happily and head for the cottages where they live.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.13.43.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.13.63.0.messag: Beware: these treasures belong to the water elementals. There are whole legions of them here, along with an ice elemental.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.13.80.0.messag: The stream flowing here is crystal clear, and something glimmers beneath its surface. You immediately reach for it and see what you have found.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.104.0.messa: Another elven hideout, but this time there is something here.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.14.0.messag: This is apparently a sacrificial circle, but I am standing in the middle and…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.32.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.49.0.messag: A few sleepyheads run out of the house, having failed to get up in time to join the expedition.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.51.0.messag: A few sleepyheads run out of the house, having failed to get up in time to join the expedition.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.15.68.0.messag: Yes, you chose well. Very well. You are a good queen.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.16.22.0.messag: On an old, rotten board, someone has written in blood: Whoever enters this territory shall be cursed forever. FOREVER.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.16.69.0.messag: You did not choose badly, but neither did you choose well. Never risk your life, even for a valuable artifact. Unfortunately…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.16.70.0.messag: So you did not change your mind.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.16.71.0.messag: You coward, do you want to take that artifact?
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.17.3.1.message: The smell of sulfur and smoke makes it clear that you have reached Hell itself, from which there is no escape. Your confidence drains away, and despair takes hold.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.17.67.0.messag: People will do anything for money. You have done very, very badly, and are unworthy to rule.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.17.95.0.messag: The sight of the resting place brings a bright smile to your face, and you forget all your troubles.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.18.27.0.messag: But how can I know that little town is not a trap?
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.18.45.0.messag: These woods are truly dark and gloomy. A perfect place for bandits and robbers.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.18.68.0.messag:
Now I must choose: a) A lot of money
                                 b) A relic
                                 c) Saving a person
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.18.89.0.messag: A deep silence hangs here. You hear only the rustle of a warm breeze and the occasional hoot of a little owl or another owl.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.19.30.0.messag: “Help! Help!” comes a cry from over there.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.19.39.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.19.95.0.messag: A tall gate towers before you, and you can already feel the magical energy coming from beyond it.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.2.36.0.message: You accidentally bump into a bandit, and he realises you are a spy…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.20.31.0.messag: The noise grows louder. You are now certain it comes from over there.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.20.91.0.messag: It is beautiful here. Considering the war raging outside, this place is truly wonderful.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.22.33.0.messag: A horrible sight greets you: an infernal creature torturing a goblin. I must intervene, I must!
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.22.46.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.22.78.0.messag: Now you know what causes the breeze and the wind… Suddenly the wind becomes a storm, and a violent downpour leaves you utterly weakened.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.23.75.0.messag: At last the storm subsides, and you see a small castle ahead. Just then, a volley of missiles flies from the treetops…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.24.5.0.message: You choose this one? Then jump in, and the decision will be made.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.24.51.0.messag: Bandits seem to be buried here.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.24.52.0.messag: As you walk around the tombs, one opens, and a gigantic monster climbs out.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.24.81.0.messag: The forest grows darker and deeper. The breeze gradually becomes a wind.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.24.90.0.messag: The dark forest is only for the very, very, very bravest.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.25.75.0.messag: The building looks quite old, but it is well maintained.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.25.88.0.messag: You feel the darkness of this forest and its cold breeze. You wonder whether to turn back.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.100.0.messa: A little man jumps out of the forest at you. You immediately recognise the guard of your castle, a very dear friend. Only now do you notice that his… mouth is sewn shut. You recoil in horror and…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.50.0.messag: A few elves run out of the forest, sent by their wise chief to help you
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.75.0.messag: A young elf rushes out of the building, scratched and covered in blood. Before you can ask him anything, several Dendroid Guards attack you.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.83.0.messag: Several monsters leap from the treetops. You form ranks and prepare for the worst.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.85.0.messag: A few archers emerge from the forest, looking happy after hunting down a fine cerberus. You ask whether they would like to continue with you, and they agree.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.26.87.0.messag: Genies suddenly appear before you and begin to attack.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.28.43.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.28.46.0.messag: A few armed men leap from the forest and demand money. To pay or not to pay?
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.28.52.0.messag: The isolated lighthouse apparently makes a good hideout for bandits.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.28.76.0.messag: Suddenly a little dragon descends from the sky and says, “You have passed a very difficult test, but the only way out is through me.” The little dragon transforms into a large dragon and…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.29.107.0.messa: They must take wonderful care of their horses here! I have never seen horses like these. The stablehand brings you the most precious one; for a few gold pieces, it is yours. You take it at once.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.29.28.0.messag: The attack was sudden and unexpected. The elves seem to have forgotten you were with them.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.3.40.0.message: You accidentally bump into a bandit, and he realises you are a spy…
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.3.82.0.message: The river must begin here. The elves seem very tidy. Not a scrap of paper or dirt anywhere. This alliance must succeed.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.30.4.0.message: You choose this one? Then jump in, and the decision will be made.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.30.54.0.messag: A whole band of bandits runs out of the lighthouse to capture you. Suddenly arrows pierce them. You turn instinctively and see a few elves, who immediately disappear again.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.30.75.1.messag: These ones apparently were not so lucky.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.31.38.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.31.42.0.messag: These woods are very mysterious. It is pitch-black here, for the dense canopy keeps sunlight from illuminating this dark place.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.31.94.0.messag: An alliance with the elves—now that would be something.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.32.50.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.34.14.0.messag: A volley of arrows flies from the forest, and a battle cry tells you bandits are nearby. You must fight! But be careful: since Deamon took command, the bandits have had high morale...
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.34.38.0.messag: It looks as though you have found a bandit’s secret hideout.

map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.71.90.0.messag: “Ow!” cries a soldier, swatting a little dragonfly. Moments later, more dragonflies arrive—much larger ones.
map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.72.36.0.messag: The sawmill also seems to be operating, but it looks rather wretched.

map.[sod] - pomsta.guards.8.93.0.message: Something like our magic tower, but smaller.

map.[sod] - pán prstenu.sign.37.31.1.mes: Here lies Balin, Lord of Moria.
A few notes:
The original film Dune, based on Frank Herbert’s novel, is now a classic. The film features the Atreides and Harkonnens but no Ordos, so I drew the main inspiration for this map from Westwood Studios’ Dune 2000 instead. But do not worry: this will be no science fiction. I borrowed only some names and the nature of the Houses.
If you are not playing multiplayer, you can change the victory condition to defeating the enemies alone.
If you find any inaccurate terms, do not keep them to yourself. Let me know so I can correct them. This is mainly for the beta testers /why did I even bother writing this, eh, Gremlin...??/.
You will find no lines like "You shall not pass!" or "That is mine!" and so on. I thought it pointless to write such things here, so the texts cover only the story, quests and information. This map is therefore certainly not compulsory "school" reading.
One more thing: do not take remarks in these brackets {//} seriously. Those are my occasional comments.

Deep in space lies a planet that at first seems utterly worthless and barren. A planet of sand, deserts, sandstorms and mysterious sandworms. Yet look closer and you will discover something found nowhere else: a strange spice. 
This planet is called Arrakis, and because of its all-pervading sand, it is also known as Dune.
Each year, one House has the right to control Dune. The Harkonnens’ term of rule is now ending, but they have refused to leave. This naturally displeases the other Houses, Atreides and Ordos. Words cannot solve this problem. War has come to Dune, the desert planet. The three mightiest Houses now fight for dominion over Dune!
"You will die on this planet! We have seen it!"

a quotation from the introduction to Dune 2000
The Atreides ambushed a Harkonnen convoy and relieved it of a small fortune!
Our finest spies infiltrated the Harkonnen headquarters and managed to steal:
An Atreides harvester was attacked and destroyed. Its spice now belongs to us!
A message has arrived from the Fremen:
"Our leader, our people have raided several enemy spice harvesters for you. In some cases, the spice has already been converted into rare resources!"
Our scout discovered an underground tunnel leading directly to the Atreides headquarters. He stole a little, but was spotted, so the Atreides immediately filled in the tunnel. Even that small fortune is certainly worthwhile!
“Leader, those honest Atreides were taking some gold and resources to the Fremen. So we relieved them of it and kept it for ourselves!”
Dune’s fierce storms are taking their toll. The main headquarters was damaged, and repairs were costly!

Your court seer jumped from the tower! Before he could leap, he shouted in confusion:

All is lost, they are everywhere, in every shadow of darkness, no one can withstand them, withstand Him... ...take everything I have, I will no longer need it... ...rather than lose my mind, my memory for ever... ...my lord, I am sorry, I have no strength left... ...rather than suffer endlessly, I will join the enemy, do not hold it against me... ...I have lost my faith. May your faith remain strong, and your army have courage...

Your hopes are in vain! Foolish mortal, your mother bore you for nothing. One day your journey will end, and I, Thant, lord of the undead, will welcome you into the ranks of my countless army. You cannot imagine how many generations of men have swelled my army since the dawn of time. For I am the one with the power to enslave their dead bodies and imprison their souls. I like strong warriors: the braver a warrior was in mortal life, the mightier he becomes in my service. So I am sending you some money, that you may become my subject with honour.

The blacksmith's body has vanished. The fat, gossiping cook said she saw him walking into the fields yesterday, without so much as looking back. When her assistant gently reminded her that the blacksmith had already gone to meet his maker, instead of blushing with shame she gasped and turned noticeably pale. She tried to stammer something, but no one could understand it, and she has not spoken since. She has gone mute. Well, at least we have some peace from her endless gossip.

The cook and her assistant have vanished. Despite her dreadful nature, you now admit that the groom cannot cook as well as she could. Sometimes he even puts beetles in the soup, claiming they are spices...

Foolish neighbours! They seem to have noticed nothing. They keep squabbling and fighting as though nothing were happening. They will pay for it. Seeing them squander their strength, you have resolved that someone must govern the whole country better, for their own good as well. And before it is too late!

Legend tells of an island domain to the north, inhabited by knights, warrior monks. Cut off from the world, they live somewhat apart. They have no dealings with anyone, and seem to have a reason for avoiding others. They are forever arming themselves, as though preparing for something.
Dreary and joyless is the underground labyrinth; a chill drifts from its exits...

You cannot escape me, Thant, master of death and eternity, you ridiculous mortal. Death will always catch you, whatever the circumstances. Everyone has a fate awaiting them, and your book of life closes tomorrow. On the one hand, I must admire your resistance thus far. On the other, your chance of victory ends tomorrow, and my subjects will welcome you into their ranks. You have only one day left to finish your task, you wretched old man. No one will help you now, forge your armour or saddle your horse. From tomorrow you will have no need to eat, you foolish pawn of fate.
Kneel before your Lord, fool. Your deeds in life have earned you no rank in my army. Take a rusty sabre and join my legion of skeletons. Wait in the mass grave until I summon you to battle.
Dreary and joyless is the underground labyrinth; your fate lies in wait there...

The animals have gone mad. You hear no birdsong and see no deer. Only the rats have acted pragmatically, fleeing the fields for your castle. They are everywhere, devouring anything not safely stored away and leaving only their pungent, mousy stench.

You decided to exterminate the rats plaguing you once and for all. You poured sulfur into their burrow entrances and burned their nests. Strangely, not one resisted. They seemed frozen stiff. When you stepped on one, it gave a dry crack and crumbled to dust, as though it were merely a little skeleton wrapped in withered skin…
I suppose I shall have to do something about those rats. Their torment has become unbearable. I will spare a little mercury and try poisoning them...
The rats never appeared again, but you cannot banish that dry cracking sound from your mind...

As far as I know, spiders have always hunted insects. So why are there so many just now? Even the old blacksmith cannot remember a summer this cold. Or has he never experienced one in all his long years?
Your armour has always been reliable and supple. It is a shame the old blacksmith died. In gratitude for his service to you and your father, you will give him a fitting funeral.

When the fires died out, you searched their stinking hiding places. Among the charred bodies you found the missing resources, along with other things they had dragged in from far and wide. Unfortunately, these included pieces of their owners, whose graves they had ransacked. The wood and sulfur had burned. Perhaps that explains why the fires were so fierce and effective: they nearly brought down your castle. Or was that the real intention, with the petty thefts merely a cover?

map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.0.d:
Your court seer jumped from the tower! Before he could leap, he shouted in confusion:

All is lost, they are everywhere, in every shadow of darkness, no one can withstand them, withstand Him... ...take everything I have, I will no longer need it... ...rather than lose my mind, my memory for ever... ...my lord, I am sorry, I have no strength left... ...rather than suffer endlessly, I will join the enemy, do not hold it against me... ...I have lost my faith. May your faith remain strong, and your army have courage...
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.1.d: Your hopes are in vain! Foolish mortal, your mother bore you for nothing. One day your journey will end, and I, Thant, lord of the undead, will welcome you into the ranks of my countless army. You cannot imagine how many generations of men have swelled my army since the dawn of time. For I am the one with the power to enslave their dead bodies and imprison their souls. I like strong warriors: the braver a warrior was in mortal life, the mightier he becomes in my service. So I am sending you some money, that you may become my subject with honour.
The blacksmith's body has vanished. The fat, gossiping cook said she saw him walking into the fields yesterday, without so much as looking back. When her assistant gently reminded her that the blacksmith had already gone to meet his maker, instead of blushing with shame she gasped and turned noticeably pale. She tried to stammer something, but no one could understand it, and she has not spoken since. She has gone mute. Well, at least we have some peace from her endless gossip.
The cook and her assistant have vanished. Despite her dreadful nature, you now admit that the groom cannot cook as well as she could. Sometimes he even puts beetles in the soup, claiming they are spices...
Foolish neighbours! They seem to have noticed nothing. They keep squabbling and fighting as though nothing were happening. They will pay for it. Seeing them squander their strength, you have resolved that someone must govern the whole country better, for their own good as well. And before it is too late!
Legend tells of an island domain to the north, inhabited by knights, warrior monks. Cut off from the world, they live somewhat apart. They have no dealings with anyone, and seem to have a reason for avoiding others. They are forever arming themselves, as though preparing for something.
Dreary and joyless is the underground labyrinth; a chill drifts from its exits...
You cannot escape me, Thant, master of death and eternity, you ridiculous mortal. Death will always catch you, whatever the circumstances. Everyone has a fate awaiting them, and your book of life closes tomorrow. On the one hand, I must admire your resistance thus far. On the other, your chance of victory ends tomorrow, and my subjects will welcome you into their ranks. You have only one day left to finish your task, you wretched old man. No one will help you now, forge your armour or saddle your horse. From tomorrow you will have no need to eat, you foolish pawn of fate.
Kneel before your Lord, fool. Your deeds in life have earned you no rank in my army. Take a rusty sabre and join my legion of skeletons. Wait in the mass grave until I summon you to battle.
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.2.d: Dreary and joyless is the underground labyrinth; your fate lies in wait there...
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.3.d: The animals have gone mad. You hear no birdsong and see no deer. Only the rats have acted pragmatically, fleeing the fields for your castle. They are everywhere, devouring anything not safely stored away and leaving only their pungent, mousy stench.
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.4.d: You decided to exterminate the rats plaguing you once and for all. You poured sulfur into their burrow entrances and burned their nests. Strangely, not one resisted. They seemed frozen stiff. When you stepped on one, it gave a dry crack and crumbled to dust, as though it were merely a little skeleton wrapped in withered skin…
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.5.d: I suppose I shall have to do something about those rats. Their torment has become unbearable. I will spare a little mercury and try poisoning them...
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.6.d: The rats never appeared again, but you cannot banish that dry cracking sound from your mind...
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.7.d: As far as I know, spiders have always hunted insects. So why are there so many just now? Even the old blacksmith cannot remember a summer this cold. Or has he never experienced one in all his long years?
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.8.d: Your armour has always been reliable and supple. It is a shame the old blacksmith died. In gratitude for his service to you and your father, you will give him a fitting funeral.
map.[sod] - stiny temnot utoci.event.9.d: When the fires died out, you searched their stinking hiding places. Among the charred bodies you found the missing resources, along with other things they had dragged in from far and wide. Unfortunately, these included pieces of their owners, whose graves they had ransacked. The wood and sulfur had burned. Perhaps that explains why the fires were so fierce and effective: they nearly brought down your castle. Or was that the real intention, with the petty thefts merely a cover?

Renowned knight, you have fought many battles, yet beware: shadows can deceive...

map.[sod] - strom 20.event.0.description: Your father died, and as his firstborn son you inherited the kingdom. No sooner had you become king than a mysterious-looking man in a black hood came to see you and said: "My name is Zoltan. I am your faithful servant and scout. I shall regularly venture out to explore and report what I learn. For now I know little. The kingdom was closed off for many years, and hardly anyone knew what was happening beyond the town walls. That was your father's policy: stay out of everything. But circumstances have changed! The world is no longer what it was. It is time to start building an army, or our kingdom may not survive." After this brief speech, Zoltan left.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.1.description: You asked your advisers about the mysterious Zoltan, but none had ever heard of him. You decided it must have been some sort of joke. What would we need an army for? Who would attack our peaceful town? You had heard of the world's other rulers, certainly, but why should they be our enemies? Even your father had never communicated with them.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.10.descriptio: Zoltan visited you at lunch today. You were dining with your wife, the queen. Sadly, for some time now you have shared only the dining table, rather than the royal bed. Whether this is because of your countless mistresses or because the queen disapproves of your aggressive policies is beside the point. All you care about is Zoltan's news. "My lord, I have learned that a seer living deep underground is willing to give Queen Catherine warriors of incredible power. If we could win her over and make her venture underground to see this mysterious man, it would certainly help us greatly against the others." You wonder why Zoltan is telling you such nonsense. No one has heard of Queen Catherine for years, and even if they had, getting her to some seer on enemy territory would be utterly impossible. This time Zoltan's information was little help, but you cannot be angry with him. You are beginning to feel that the two of you are becoming good friends.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.11.descriptio: During today's visit, Zoltan tells you of an island full of treasures and artifacts. You heard this legend from your nurse as a child, but what if it is true? Zoltan says he has never seen the island himself, but knows from reliable sources that it really exists and can only be reached through a portal. You are fascinated, and begin dreaming of how wonderful it would be to visit this island, and how much power it would bring you.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.12.descriptio: Early in the morning, one of your advisers came to see you and said: "My lord, I overheard your conversation with Zoltan yesterday. You were talking about the island of treasure, were you not?" You are rather annoyed that he dares to listen to your private conversation and then question you about it. Still, you are curious about his news, so you nod and he continues: "I know the Dungeon rulers are our enemies, and I would never dare communicate with anyone from their kingdoms without your orders, but something interesting happened yesterday. I was drinking in the town tavern when I saw a stranger. I had already downed several large tankards of beer, so I struck up a conversation. He claimed to have lived in an underground town, but fled to avoid joining the army and fighting the alliance of surface rulers. We also spoke of the island of treasure. Besides repeating what Zoltan told you yesterday, he claimed that the orange ruler has his kingdom on that island." This truly surprises you. It seems the island of treasure is real, and inhabited too. If the mysterious orange ruler enjoys all the island's advantages, he could be incredibly powerful. You wonder how far you can trust some tavern drunk, especially one who comes from those mangy Dungeon dwellers underground...
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.13.descriptio: Although you are already convinced that your kingdom can survive only by ridding the world of your opponents, at the wishes of your advisers and the queen you decided to send envoys to the other kingdoms offering an alliance. Perhaps it is not such a bad idea, you think. Despite the mutual hostility, perhaps one of the surface rulers, or even an underground ruler, has some sense and will wish to join us. You sent nothing to "Orange", since none of your envoys knows exactly where the island of treasure lies. Even if they did, they would not return alive. Every small child knows that invincible monsters guard the legendary island of treasure.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.14.descriptio: Today the replies to your alliance offers arrived. You had not expected them so soon. All 4 messengers came on the same day, one from each ruler. You had expected your own envoys to bring the answers, but in the end you were pleased. Your messengers must have been tired from their journey and could hardly have returned so quickly. As soon as each of the four messengers handed you a letter and a package, he mounted his steed and galloped out of town. You thought: "That is how it should be done. No dawdling: deliver the message and return straight to your master. My lazy fellows are surely getting drunk in some tavern among our enemies. It will be days before they come back." You accepted the letters and packages yourself, eager to discover which rulers had accepted your offer. But the letters shocked you! They were much alike: nothing but threats, obscenities and boasts about conquering our kingdom. In fury, you threw them all into the fireplace and picked up the first package. The moment you opened it and looked inside, you realised there was no point opening the rest... You knew the Dungeon rulers were depraved, but had not expected this from those on the surface. It could mean only one thing: conquer the entire world, or see our kingdom fall. You flung the package aside, and as it struck the floor, your messenger's head rolled out.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.15.descriptio: After a long absence, Zoltan visited you again and encouraged your decision to destroy the others and conquer their kingdoms. He also told you that their armies were very powerful, so the situation must not be underestimated.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.16.descriptio: Today Zoltan tells you what he overheard among the members of the scouts' guild. "My lord, I have reports of a town underground inhabited solely by dragons guarding immense riches. However, their town can be reached only through special spells." Although the news interests you, you would rather learn more about the island of treasure, particularly the "orange" ruler who apparently has his kingdom there. Zoltan merely repeats what you already know: the island holds untold riches, and the only way there is through a portal. He refuses to discuss the orange ruler, claiming never even to have heard of him.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.17.descriptio: This is outrageous! One of your advisers dared criticise your decision to fight the other rulers and attempt to conquer their towns. You immediately had him arrested and sent to the quarry for the hardest labour. This caused less outrage than you expected. The other advisers now mostly support your policies, and public opinion is on your side too. The question remains whether this is because you have shown that even a senior adviser can be harshly punished for speaking against the king, or because everyone is truly beginning to believe in what you do for the people.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.18.descriptio: This time Zoltan interrupted your conversation with your strongest hero, whom you had visited personally for a report on the current situation and your army. If anyone conquers the other rulers' towns, it will be him. You introduce him to Zoltan, who jokingly offers to join your army and fight the enemy himself. You and your chief hero laugh. You decline with thanks, but praise Zoltan's courage and draw him aside to hear his news. Zoltan says the underground rulers are stronger than those on the surface. It is only a matter of time before they conquer the surface towns, after which stopping them will be very difficult. He advises you to defeat the "surface alliance" yourself, then destroy the underground rulers using armies from your newly conquered towns.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.19.descriptio: You learned that an amateur theatre in your kingdom was staging a satire mocking the current political situation. So one day you secretly attended, disguised as an ordinary townsman. Yes, it was undoubtedly funny, but unfortunately it mocked both you and Zoltan. The playwright even went so far as to include a scene in which an actor delivers a monologue suggesting that Zoltan's frequent late-night visits to your palace have a sexual undertone. So despite your kingdom's freedom of speech and your own sense of humour, you decided to send the author and the actors playing you and Zoltan to the quarry for the hardest labour, and had the theatre closed. No one treats the king like that!
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.2.description: Zoltan has returned. What a surprise. He tells you of his journey: "I have contacts in the scouts' guild and have learned something. Only 6 rulers remain in this world, my lord. In your father's day there were 14, and it seems they are fighting and conquering one another's kingdoms." Your response is somewhat lukewarm. You know little about the outside world, but your advisers have already told you that it is divided among 6 rulers. Why does Zoltan tell you such useless things? You send him away. If only he would do something useful instead. You have heard that the quarry needs more workers. He would certainly be more use there...
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.20.descriptio: Since the recent incident at the theatre, protests among some of your subjects have multiplied. They complain that freedom of speech is being violated and that everyone was better off under your father. These remarks are beginning to annoy you considerably. Yes, perhaps we were better off before, but now we are at war. If we lose, the people will learn what hardship truly means. They will become slaves to one of this world's ruthless rulers. You therefore decided to issue a decree changing the existing royal laws. The new laws strictly forbid any deed, word or even thought against the king, his family and the royal advisers. You also raised taxes, since war is expensive, and declared yourself an absolute monarch with unlimited power. These measures will surely silence even your government's worst detractors.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.21.descriptio: Zoltan visited you at night again today. He praised your firm treatment of your subjects and your conduct of the war. For the first time in a while, you asked about the island of treasure, but learned nothing again. Instead, you felt he grew slightly nervous. He quickly said goodbye and left in his characteristic fashion: by jumping out of the window.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.22.descriptio: Zoltan's visit yesterday did little to please you. You are glad he supports your decisions, but above all you expect information, which has been in short supply lately. You remembered that on his first visit Zoltan mentioned your father. Could they have known each other? If so, why has Zoltan said nothing about it?
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.23.descriptio: You keep wondering whether Zoltan knew your father. Next time he appears, you will certainly ask. At any rate, he cannot have been one of his advisers. Zoltan looks younger than you, and your father would never have hired anyone so young. Besides, you would probably have known him, as you knew most of your father's former advisers. To be sure, you ordered one of your advisers to check the royal library's archives. You expect little, however. Over the centuries, an incredible amount of information has accumulated there. Even if a record of Zoltan exists, it would be very hard to find, particularly since the archives are in an unbelievable state of disorder.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.24.descriptio: "Ah, speak of the devil," you think as Zoltan enters your dining room in the middle of lunch. Your guards would plainly have admitted no one else, but Zoltan now enjoys certain privileges. You tell him to join your family at the royal table. The queen gives you a reproachful look, but Zoltan is already seated and helping himself to the royal cook's speciality: troll brains. He jokes that he is surprised trolls have brains at all. You have not seen him in such good spirits for a long time, so you begin asking about the island of treasure. This time Zoltan replies with icy calm that he has no information. Undeterred, you ask when he was born and where he comes from. Zoltan suddenly chokes badly, and after a moment coughs up a small piece of troll brain. "Forgive me, my lord, but I must go. Next time I shall certainly bring important information," he says, and leaves at a brisk pace. You cannot shake the feeling that your "faithful servant Zoltan", as he likes to call himself, is surrounded by far too many mysteries.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.25.descriptio: The adviser you sent to search the archives for records of Zoltan came to see you. "My lord, I have spent several days carefully searching for any mention, but found nothing at all." Naturally, the news displeased you. Much to his dismay, you sent him back to keep searching, though you know it will most likely achieve nothing.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.26.descriptio: Today, after a long time, Zoltan brought fresh news. He claims that six castles belonging to the Dungeon rulers lie hidden underground. That is more than you expected. Clearly their army will be very strong. Although the news is hardly encouraging, you are pleased that Zoltan is useful again, and order him to discover further details about the underground.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.27.descriptio: The royal theatre is celebrating its grand reopening. After the recent unpleasant incident forced its lengthy closure, little interest in the new play was expected. Yet the opposite proved true. The cream of the entire kingdom gathered for the gala premiere, led by you, their highly respected and beloved king. As you and the queen approached the theatre entrance, a great crowd of subjects gathered around, cheering your name. Some even tried to touch you, so your personal guards had to intervene and drag the fanatics away. The play was gripping. It told of a kingdom at war with others which won a magnificent victory through its king's military genius. Although the characters' names resembled no one in the real world, you clearly saw that the similarities to reality were considerable. You were therefore delighted, and even became the first to rise for a standing ovation. The actors' faces showed immense relief, naturally enough: had the previous fiasco been repeated, every last one of them would have ended up in the quarry, and you would have closed the theatre for good. Fortunately, the actors had learned their lesson, allowing this splendid ode to your magnificent deeds to be created.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.28.descriptio: When Zoltan visited today, he clearly wanted to tell you something, yet avoided it and spoke only of trivial matters. After a while of boring chatter, you snapped at him to tell the truth and stop keeping you from your royal duties. Zoltan took a deep breath and began: "My lord, I apologise for concealing my origins, but I feared your reaction. It is an immense honour to serve you, and I would hate to lose that opportunity..." You suddenly interrupt and demand that he get to the point. Zoltan draws breath again and continues: "Very well. The truth is that I come from an underground town ruled by the underground alliance. But as soon as I learned of their intention to conquer this world, I knew I could not side with them. Although I was originally one of them, I know the underground represents evil, and I want nothing to do with them. I preferred to join your side and help you fight them. I am sorry I did not tell you sooner, but I feared you would consider me a spy and refuse my services." Zoltan's words please you. You are glad he is honest with you and that you have uncovered at least one part of his mysterious past. Of course, you would rather he had confided in you sooner, but better now than never.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.29.descriptio: Rumours are beginning to circulate in certain circles that the queen is unfaithful to you. Some even claim that her lover is your good friend Zoltan himself. These are surely inventions, yet the reports still anger you considerably. You need a scout to get to the bottom of it. Normally Zoltan would be the obvious choice, but clearly that is a poor idea in this case. So you assign one of your advisers to follow the queen in secret. Perhaps you will learn the truth.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.3.description: While you spoke with Zoltan yesterday, your advisers watched from a distance. You asked whether they recognised him. Even the older ones, who knew all your father's advisers and scouts, had never seen him.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.30.descriptio: The adviser you recently ordered to follow the queen returned to report. "My lord, I watched the queen day and night, but discovered nothing unusual. It seems these were merely rumours spread by an opponent to ridicule you before your subjects." This did not surprise you. It was more or less what you expected, but you must still speak to the queen. You visit her chamber and apologise for suspecting her of infidelity. Unexpectedly, the queen bursts into tears and begins apologising to you. She says she invented the rumours herself and ordered her lady-in-waiting to spread them among the people. You cannot believe your ears. You ask why she would do such a thing. She tells you how unhappy she was when you decided to wage war against the other rulers, and especially when she learned that you were betraying her with so many other women. She says she would never dare be unfaithful, but made up these lies so you could understand her suffering. After she speaks, you approach with a sympathetic expression. She smiles, but you immediately slap her so hard she falls to the floor, and begin shouting: "How could you dare do this to me!? It is unforgivable!" You storm away to write an order sending the queen's lady-in-waiting to hard labour in the quarry.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.31.descriptio: You reflect on yesterday's incident. The queen should not have done this to you. You would dearly like to send her to the quarry too: you have the authority, but decide that would be going too far. The people are extremely loyal to you, at least according to your advisers' surveys, but everyone loves the queen. You therefore decide to conceal the whole affair. You and the queen will play the ideal royal couple, though reality is precisely the opposite. The whole thing is rather stressful, so you send an adviser to fetch your favourite prostitute.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.32.descriptio: Zoltan visited today. You are glad he came, for the last few days have been difficult. You poured some fine wine and talked at length. You told him of your progress in conquering the other towns and the growth of your army. Zoltan strongly encouraged your efforts and admired your leadership. You drank a great deal, and although you are no novice at drinking, you began to sway considerably. Seeing this, Zoltan said he had better leave. You tried to persuade him to stay, saying the fun was only beginning, but he bade you farewell and, showing not the slightest sign of drunkenness, departed once again in his characteristic manner: by jumping out of the window.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.33.descriptio: An adviser you had not seen for many days came to you. He was the one you sent to the archives to find information on Zoltan. "What were you doing there so long?" you ask the rather haggard man. "My lord, every day I spent 14 hours examining records and still found nothing. Only today did I discover 2 records concerning Zoltan: a birth certificate and a court record stating that he was charged with robbery." You are astonished, not only by the charge but especially by the birth certificate. You know Zoltan comes from underground, not our town, so there can be only one explanation: this is another Zoltan. The name is unusual, but the kingdom has many inhabitants. Someone might share it. You respond accordingly: "So you hid in the archives for weeks just to find someone with the same name? You are asking for a job in the quarry." But the adviser interrupts: "My lord, I am certain this is the very Zoltan you sent me to investigate," and hands you the court file, bearing Zoltan's portrait. Though the paper is rather damaged, Zoltan looks exactly as he does now, so clearly the file must be relatively recent. You do not feel like reading the lengthy proceedings, so ask how old it is and whether Zoltan was convicted. The adviser scratches his head. "The whole affair is more than strange. It took so long to find anything because, to be thorough, I searched even the closed sections of the archives." You ask what he means, and he continues: "My lord, Zoltan was convicted, but that is hardly the point. Something else matters more, and I truly cannot explain it. The court file is over 100 years old, and according to the birth certificate, Zoltan was born 130 years ago!"
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.34.descriptio: You spent the entire night reading and rereading both files from the archives. It is utterly unbelievable. According to the birth certificate, Zoltan was born to ordinary townsfolk in a house opposite the town tavern. That is all you know so far. The court file offers more: Zoltan and three accomplices robbed a cart carrying gems from the mine to the royal treasury. They made off with several thousand gold pieces' worth of loot, but were soon caught. All except Zoltan received 10 years in the town dungeon. Zoltan refused to cooperate or confess, had planned the robbery, and even attempted to escape custody, earning himself 12 years of labour in the quarry. (Clearly this punishment was in use long before your reign.) Yet the portrait frightens you most. It is exactly the Zoltan you have known for several months. You must obtain more information. Finding anyone who remembers those days will plainly be difficult, but you nevertheless order all your advisers to search the town for citizens who heard of Zoltan before he came to our kingdom just before the war.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.35.descriptio: Your advisers do nothing but walk the town asking everyone about Zoltan. Getting sensible information is rather difficult. Almost everyone knows him, but certainly as the king's respected adviser, rather than a convict. So when the advisers ask whether anyone knows who Zoltan was and what he did over 100 years ago, people take it as a poor joke.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.36.descriptio: After several days of questioning, your advisers found an old man who claimed to remember Zoltan and recognised his portrait in the file. You go to question him personally. Entering his home, you see an old man whom death will soon claim. One of your personal guards leans towards you and says his name is Malcolm. According to the archives, he is 108 years old, making him our kingdom's oldest inhabitant. You ask what he can tell you about Zoltan. The old man sits up painfully in bed and speaks in a hoarse voice: "My lord, I remember Zoltan's case, although I was only a small boy then. My father worked as a guard in the quarry and often took me along. One day the prisoners rebelled, and several tried to escape. Zoltan was among them. I remember him because he was the one who killed my father. It was unbelievable, and I still see it as though it were yesterday. All the prisoners were trying to fight through a squad of guards, wielding their stone-breaking tools as weapons. All except Zoltan, who was hurling powerful spells around him! One struck my father, and he fell. I ran to help him, but it was too late. I could only watch his murderer fleeing the quarry while the other guards ruthlessly executed the remaining rebels, whose tools stood no chance against sharp swords." "How is this possible? Why do I know nothing of this? Why do none of my advisers?" you shout, filling the house. The old man continues: "Times were different then. A prison revolt was unthinkable, let alone a successful escape, especially by someone wielding powerful magic. It would have caused widespread panic and distrust of the king. No one could be allowed to learn of it. No one missed the dead prisoners. My father's death was officially called an accident, and the whole event was never entered in the archives. Even as a little boy, I had to swear before the king himself, your great-grandfather, my lord, that I would never speak of it. Although today the event would surely be public knowledge, and few would think twice about it, I have kept my oath all my life. Of course, I had no idea your new adviser was that criminal." You are stunned. Without a word, you leave to reflect in your chambers.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.37.descriptio: You could not sleep all night, and since morning have been discussing your next move with your advisers. You reject their recommendation to have Zoltan killed, or at least arrested, as soon as he appears in the kingdom. He is your friend, after all. There must be a reasonable explanation for the mystery. But what!? You ought to calm down. Stress is bad for you. So you have your royal blacksmith's beautiful young daughter brought to your bedchamber. She will know how to ease your worries.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.38.descriptio: Still no sign of Zoltan. It is as though he knows you have many questions and will not be brushed aside. You can do nothing but wait. At least you are studying battle tactics and overseeing the training of new warriors. The enemy never sleeps!
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.39.descriptio: Tired of waiting for Zoltan, you decided to pass the time by organising the traditional tournament in your favourite card game. The finest players from far and wide came to the kingdom to compete for the enormous winner's prize of 1000 gold pieces. You entered yourself and played splendidly, eliminating opponent after opponent until, with enthusiastic support from the audience, you reached the final. Your opponent was very good and controlled the game throughout, but at the crucial moment he made a fatal mistake. You seized the opportunity and soon brought the game to a victorious close. The tournament is yours, and you are delighted, since last year you were knocked out in the first round.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.4.description: Zoltan visited again, this time at night. He appeared in your chamber, you know not how, and shared his news: "My lord, you already know there are 5 rival rulers in this world whom you should fear." You are unconvinced. So far you have no reason to fear an attack by another ruler, but you let Zoltan continue: "I have learned that some of the rulers have allied to conquer the world together. I believe it will not be long before they attack our kingdom too."
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.40.descriptio: A few malcontents are spoiling yesterday's victory by spreading rumours that your opponents let you win. It is absurd, of course. They have no proof. Their sole, ridiculous argument is that last year you had the fingers of the opponent who eliminated you cut off. But you did that only in a momentary fit of rage. Everyone knows a calm, level-headed king like you would never order such a thing again. Surely these are the same slanderers who objected to the tournament prize coming from the treasury. They will always complain; there is no pleasing them. Furious, you send word to the quarry overseer: you have more workers for him.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.41.descriptio: It has been many days since Zoltan last appeared in your kingdom. You are impatient, and have even prepared a speech listing all the mysterious facts with which you intend to confront him. But what use is that when you simply do not know where he is? You have had enough, and decide to send your three best spies to find him. The world is vast and their chances are slim, but your curiosity is too strong to let you simply forget all these mysteries surrounding Zoltan.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.42.descriptio: "Excellent!" you exclaimed sarcastically on reading that the first of your three spies was dead. He had been travelling by ship and accidentally fallen overboard when it entered a whirlpool. You hope the other two spies will prove less clumsy.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.43.descriptio: Today you read more unwelcome news about the spies you recently dispatched. One of the two remaining men was captured by wandering nomads. They demand a ransom of 1000 gold pieces if you wish to see him alive again. Enraged by their insolence, you write that unless they release him immediately, your men will find them and kill them all.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.44.descriptio: Another message arrived from the extortionate nomads. Untroubled by your threats, they have chosen to become harsher themselves. Not only have they raised their demand to 2000 gold pieces, but they enclosed a small "gift": your spy's severed ear. You do not know why, but the ear stirred a little compassion, and you decided to free your subject. You send the nomads 150 gold pieces, which will surely satisfy them and inspire them to release your spy with immense gratitude. Going to bed that evening, you reflect on your kindness and love for your subjects, and consider adopting the epithet "the Merciful".
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.45.descriptio: Your generous gift evidently failed to satisfy the nomads. At least, that is what you conclude when they send your spy's severed head instead of a letter of thanks and the freed man. You surprise yourself by taking it calmly, without much anger. Smiling, you order a band of elite warriors to find the kidnappers' camp and slaughter everyone there, including the women and children. They are then to bring the children's heads back to town and impale them on stakes along the walls.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.46.descriptio: You have dealt with the nomads, but the Zoltan affair remains at a standstill. He has not visited of his own accord for many weeks, and only one spy remains to find him, with no word of his whereabouts. You can only wait patiently. To make the waiting pass more quickly, you decide to establish a personal harem, where you will surely find something else to think about.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.47.descriptio: At last your final spy returned. He was still breathless when brought before you, but you wasted no time asking what he had learned. "My lord, I achieved something incredible: I reached the island of treasure!" For a moment you simply stare in disbelief, but soon demand every detail. The spy continues: "I slipped past every obstacle unnoticed and travelled through a portal to an island where I saw immeasurable riches. I immediately thought it must be the legendary island of treasure. Monsters were everywhere, so I did not linger, but before returning something very strange happened. From the moment I arrived, I felt someone watching me. I tried to discover whether I was imagining it, but saw no one. It was just a strange feeling. Then, just before entering the portal, I took one last look around and saw someone watching me from behind a tree..." The spy pauses, but your patience runs out. "Who?!" you shout. He answers: "Zoltan, my lord, Zoltan... He was some distance away, and I saw him only briefly, but that piercing gaze is unforgettable. It was him." You are stunned. Without a word, you leave to reflect quietly in your chambers and try to understand what it all means.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.48.descriptio: You keep thinking about the spy's testimony yesterday, but you must also direct a very difficult war. Holding the towns you have conquered is no easy matter. Better to concentrate on taking the remaining ones than on thoughts of Zoltan. Perhaps he will appear of his own accord, and you will finally understand the mystery surrounding him.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.49.descriptio: A cockerel's crow wakes you. It is morning. You yawn, rub your eyes and suddenly see a human figure beside your bed. You strain to focus your blurred vision and recognise Zoltan. You draw breath to call the guards, but he springs forward, covers your mouth and presses a knife to your throat. He indicates what will happen if you cry for help. Clearly you have no choice, so you nod your agreement. Zoltan puts the knife away and begins quietly: "We have little time, but I have decided to satisfy your boundless curiosity. I know I am taking a great risk, but seeing surprise and terror in your eyes will be worth it. You have been my puppet all along. Everything you decided was influenced by what I told you. In fact, this entire war is happening because of your naivety and gullibility." Zoltan is right. You are shocked, and your expression shows it. You replay every meeting in your mind, trying to assemble the puzzle. Zoltan is clearly amused by your bewilderment. He waits a moment for you to speak, but you merely stare silently into his cold eyes. So he continues: "Perhaps I should never have told you of the island of treasure. It stirred more interest than I expected. I merely wanted to give you a reason to advance underground with your army and fight its rulers." You still do not understand... You thought he supported your war because he was on your side, but now you see his intentions were entirely different. You hunger for the truth. Wearing a smile unlike any you have seen on him before, Zoltan continues: "The truth is, you were never my master. That honour belongs, now and always, solely to Lord Orhsabaal: King of the Undead, Father of Vampires, Terror of the Living and the Dead, Despoiler of Men, Grand Master of Necromancy, Devourer of Souls, Death Knight..." Zoltan continues reciting his king's titles for some time, but you no longer listen. You have just realised his master is the orange ruler. Suddenly everything makes more sense. Yet you still have many questions, so you interrupt his introduction of Lord Orhsabaal and demand that he get to the point. Zoltan finishes his ode and resumes his explanation: "My master's priorities are clear: he wants to conquer this land and every town in it. Yet despite his army's tremendous strength, he cannot leave his island. Powerful curses keep him and his army trapped in the town. So my master devised a brilliant plan: stir up war among this world's rulers, wait for them to slaughter one another, then kill the last survivors and seize every town." "And how will you manage that if the army cannot leave the town?" you ask provocatively, adding a smirk. Surprisingly, Zoltan no longer frightens you as much as before. "Lord Orhsabaal is a mighty sorcerer and works tirelessly to break the curse. My visits throughout the war prove that he has already achieved partial success. An individual can leave the town with relatively little trouble, but his vast army cannot yet do so. Nevertheless, I know he will ultimately overcome every obstacle." Zoltan pauses, watching you proudly with his mysterious eyes. Thoughts race through your head. You know only that you must use his presence to extract as much information as possible. He clearly enjoys boasting, a habit that has proved fatal to more than one man. So you ask: "Why approach me? Or did you play the same game with every ruler in this world?" Malice and mockery colour his voice: "At first I tried to infiltrate the other rulers' courts, but without success. They were all very cautious. Discovery was a risk I could not take. I was beginning to fear I would fail my master, but then I learned of your father's death. I knew he would quickly see through my trickery, and I would have been lucky to leave his town alive. You were another matter: a young, naive fop drunk on power. As you noticed, persuading you to start a war took little effort. My master's plan is proceeding smoothly. Though you think you can hold your towns, perhaps even defeat him, you are gravely mistaken." Zoltan's mockery offends you. A naive fop, you? You reassure yourself that you are your people's beloved, infallible ruler, who will lead them to victory in this war. Surely you would have started it without Zoltan, since your people's welfare and the conquest of enemy towns are your calling. You have more questions. You tell him about the archive record showing he was in the town long before your birth. Smiling, he explains with obvious pleasure: "Yes, were I an ordinary mortal like you, I would have died long ago. But my master initiated me into the secrets of necromancy, and through his teachings I cheated death! I can also use spells to alter my physical appearance, so convincing you I was a hundred years or so younger was no trouble." He is clearly mocking you again, but you refuse to be provoked and ask another question. Why is he telling you all this? Why reveal his plan? He has plainly prepared his answer: "As I said: to see fear in your eyes. To see your reaction when confronted with reality. To see your face when you realise you were merely a puppet in my master Lord Orhsabaal's plan. Our cause faces no risk, for with our army, victory is already assured." You prepare to protest that you feel no fear, were no puppet, and that victory remains undecided. But Zoltan does not wait. His desire plainly satisfied, he turns and leaps out of your bedchamber window. You immediately summon the guards and order them to pursue him.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.5.description: You ponder what Zoltan told you yesterday. What if he is right? Although your advisers remain unconvinced, you begin building an army not only to capture mines and artifacts for your heroes, but also to defend against other rulers if necessary.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.50.descriptio: The guards you sent after Zoltan did not return until the next day. Their commander reports that they found no trace leading to him, let alone caught sight of him. You begin shouting: "How is that possible?! I sent you after him the moment he fled! And why did you only return today? What were you doing all night? You can hardly find much in the dark, can you?!" "My lord," the commander replies, "we tried to find the slightest trace, even through the night. Our chances were slim, of course, but we feared returning sooner lest you be angry that we had not searched enough. We had no wish to end up in the quarry." Calmly, you reply: "Of course I will not send you to the quarry. Why would I? You are only doing your job... But you are doing it badly! I will not tolerate my guards idling in the woods at night when they are needed chiefly in town! Still, as I promised, I will not send you to the quarry. Now get out of my sight." The commander thanks you for your generosity, bowing repeatedly even as he leaves. Once he is gone, you sit at your desk and write an order sending the other members of the search party to the quarry. You also summon the executioner and arrange the commander's execution for tomorrow... Because promises must be kept.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.51.descriptio: Naturally, over the last few days you have thought of little but Zoltan's final visit. You remain certain of your decisions, yet what you recently learned troubles you greatly. After much reflection, you make your final decision: you will not wait for the orange ruler to leave the island and begin conquering your towns. You must face him and attack. You know it will be a hard fight, that the decisive battle may be the greatest ever fought, and that losses on both sides will be enormous. But you have no choice. You know you will be the victor. You know your destiny is to become the sole ruler of this world. You know you alone will rule the Tree!
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.6.description: It is early morning, and someone is pounding on your chamber door. Who could it be, when you ordered everyone not to disturb you so you could finally sleep well? Why even ask, when you know the answer? You open the door, and of course Zoltan stands there. He says he now knows which alliances the rulers have formed. One unites two rulers on the mainland's surface; the other consists of very powerful Dungeon monarchs whose kingdoms lie underground. You ask about the final ruler. Does he not wish to join either strong alliance? For a moment Zoltan stares silently at the floor, then quietly mutters that he must discover something else, and jumps out of the window. "What a madman. A pity my chamber is not in a tower," you think, amused by your own joke, and go back for another nap.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.7.description: Zoltan visited again. It is becoming routine. You ask whether he has any information about the fifth ruler, of whom you know only that his flag is deep orange. Zoltan changes the subject. He tells you of towns currently more or less deserted, which would make useful additions to your kingdom. But you have known all this nonsense for ages. There used to be 14 rulers, so naturally some towns remain to conquer. Again you ask about the "orange ruler", but Zoltan merely shakes his head and leaves, saying he has no information. Something seems wrong. "Could my faithful servant Zoltan be hiding something from me?" you wonder.
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.8.description: Zoltan has gone too far this time! Interrupting your royal bath! He appeared beside the tub, you know not how. You are furious. How dare he look upon the naked king? Luckily, you have nothing to be ashamed of. Zoltan calmly waits for you to stop shouting, then begins: "My lord, although the other kingdoms are busy fighting one another, there is a real danger that they will attack this town too. I have great faith in your military abilities, and believe attack is the best defence. We should strike the nearest ruler. I think we have a good chance of taking his capital. His ally is far away and surely will not come to his aid." You cannot say why, but his words affect you deeply. You realise you are unlike your father: a coward who never left his town gates in his entire life. Suddenly you understand that you were born a conqueror!
map.[sod] - strom 20.event.9.description: You tell your advisers of Zoltan's visit and your decision to try to conquer the neighbouring ruler's kingdom. They are horrified, saying Zoltan is a bad influence on you. But what do they know of warfare? Nothing! All they can do is repeat their rubbish about peace and how well the people lived under your father. But you know the people did not live well. They only thought they did, because they knew no other life... And that must change! You silence your advisers by declaring that anyone opposing your decision will be sent to work in the quarry. You are already planning your attack.
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.5.101.1.mess: You may have defeated our slaves, but you will not get past us.
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.68.66.0.mess: A large band of fearsome knights approached you, claiming to have escaped Zoltan's army and offering to help you fight.
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.71.56.0.mess: I found that clover first. You will have to fight me for it.
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.77.87.1.mess: You really should have looked around more carefully this time. This will not be as easy as those battles just now.
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.82.63.0.mess: If you want our wings, you will have to kill us!
map.[sod] - strom 20.guards.90.69.0.mess: At last! This must be the legendary island of treasure.
